newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: New Colombian vice president looks to heal rifts.
newsitem.headline: New Colombian vice president looks to heal rifts.

text.p: Colombia's vice president-elect Carlos Lemos Simmonds was scheduled to hold talks with embattled President Ernesto Samper on Saturday amid hopes he may help to solve the country's political crisis.
Lemos arrived back in Colombia on Friday evening from his post as ambassador to London, telling journalists that "the vice president should represent a point of agreement not of rupture."

Lemos was formally elected by Congress last week after his predecessor, Humberto de la Calle, resigned, citing Samper's alleged links to drug kingpins and the government's deepening credibility crisis.

De la Calle used the largely ceremonial post of vice president to launch repeated attacks on Samper, stemming from allegations that the Cali drug cartel pumped millions of dollars into the president's winning 1994 election campaign.

Lemos is known as a fervent anti-guerrilla and anti-drug crusader, and it is widely hoped that he may help reimpose the rule of law at a time when leftist guerrillas are unleashing their bloodiest nationwide offensive in decades.
"Efforts should be directed at reestablishing calm and boosting public order. Neither of these aims should be subject to party politics," Lemos said.
It is not yet clear, however, whether Samper intends to ask Lemos to remain in Colombia after he officially takes office on Tuesday or whether he will return to his ambassador's post in London.
